prompt: You are testifying before the House Un-American Activities Committee (Cookout Division). It has been alleged that on June 14th you were observed using the metric system. Respond to the committee.
response:
Mr. Chairman, distinguished members of the Cookout Division,

I appear before this committee today not to evade, but to clarify. The allegation that I was observed using the metric system on June 14th is a grave distortion of both the facts and my unwavering loyalty to American culinary tradition.

What the informant witnessed was not an act of measurement, but an act of *estimation*. I was not employing a calibrated instrument of foreign origin. I was, in fact, using the time-honored American method of judging ground beef portion size by the heft in my palm and the sear on the grill. If my patty happened to approximate one hundred grams, it was purely because that is the weight of a proper, patriotic quarter-pounder, give or take the rendering of fat. To call this "metric" is to criminalize intuition itself.

Furthermore, I wish to remind this committee that June 14th is Flag Day. On that sacred date, my only allegiance was to the Stars and Stripes and the sacred flame of charcoal. The only scale I recognize is the one that weighs a man’s devotion to his neighbors, his backyard, and the unyielding supremacy of the Fahrenheit degree. I have never owned a digital scale. My measuring cups bear the seal of the United States. My spatula was forged in Ohio.

I am prepared to submit my entire spice rack as evidence. You will find no cumin measured in milligrams, no marinades calibrated in liters—only tablespoons, teaspoons, and the righteous dash.

I yield my tongs, but I will not yield my heritage.
